name: Boring liquidation reselling (pallets/returns)
one_liner: Buy unglamorous overstock and returns (plumbing fixtures, rugs, patio furniture, books) cheaply at liquidation auctions and resell them locally or on marketplaces.
customer: Local buyers, house flippers, remodelers and contractors, plus eBay and Facebook Marketplace shoppers
offer: Discounted new or returned goods such as toilets, rugs, patio furniture, pressure washers and books
how_it_makes_money: Spread between the auction price and the resale price. One example was 10 toilets that retail at $823 each, bought as a lot for $750 and resold at about half retail.
startup_cost: low to medium: $0 (free items) up to $200–$2,800 per lot, more for a full truckload
time_to_first_revenue: days. One seller made $1,200 in 13 days, and a truckload paid itself back within 36 hours
evidence: Joe went from $1,200 in his first 13 days to $17,300 in sales this month, selling from his garage (VmhEvIB_XNA)
67 rugs worth $11,000 bought for $200; two pallets of books bought for $1 and sold for $5,000 on eBay (VmhEvIB_XNA)
A Sacramento member sold 600 pressure washers, and his first patio furniture truckload made back its cost within 36 hours (W5oUjuoHWhA)
10 toilets that retail at $823 each sold as a lot for $750 (W5oUjuoHWhA)
risks: Needs storage space and physical handling
US auction sites and examples; UK equivalents and shipping costs need checking
Lots can contain damaged stock
Selling and collection happen in person

name: Christmas light installation service
one_liner: A seasonal service that designs, installs, maintains and takes down holiday lights for homes and commercial properties.
customer: Homeowners in better-off areas and commercial property owners
offer: Holiday lighting installed, serviced during the season and taken down, with lights supplied
how_it_makes_money: About $1,500–$2,000 per average home, and commercial jobs can be worth up to 100 times more. Repeat customers lift margins to 50–60% because the lights are reused.
startup_cost: low to medium: ladder, lights, insurance
evidence: A grounds operator does $1.25M in Christmas lights alone (WydE1wzv2_Y)
Margins can rise to 50 and 60% with repeat customers (WydE1wzv2_Y)
risks: Liability from working at height
Highly seasonal
UK demand and willingness to pay are likely lower than in the US
Physical, in-person work unless subcontracted

name: AI implementation and scribe retainer for professional practices
one_liner: A done-for-you service that uses AI voice recording and transcription to replace scribes and manual data entry for dentists, lawyers and small business owners.
customer: Dentists, lawyers, doctors and small business office managers
offer: Setting up and managing AI note-taking and admin automation (Make or Zapier style)
how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainer, with $1,500 a month pitched as the alternative to paying a scribe
startup_cost: low: software subscriptions and a recording device
evidence: "It's $1,500 a month and you won't need a scribe anymore" (WwR35MbyOMY)
Observed a dentist's office manager keying data in by hand, a case for automation (WwR35MbyOMY)
risks: UK GDPR and health data compliance (NHS, SRA)
Pricing is hypothetical, with no real case shown
Some calls and onboarding are needed

name: Local email newsletter
one_liner: A newsletter for a town of 50,000–100,000 people, grown with paid social ads and paid for by local sponsors and affiliate links.
customer: Local businesses buying ad placements; readers subscribe free
offer: Sponsored placements and affiliate links in a local news and events email
how_it_makes_money: Sponsorship and affiliate revenue. "The more you publish, the more you can charge."
startup_cost: low: email platform plus a modest ad budget
time_to_first_revenue: unknown, likely 1–3 months to reach a list sponsors will pay for
evidence: Built live from zero to first subscribers for Roswell, NM; model is ads → subscribers → sponsors (Y0MRAjVp_Uo)
risks: No revenue figures given
Selling to local sponsors takes outreach
Writing it is a weekly commitment
Could replicate per town, e.g. a UK town or a Portuguese-community edition

name: Marketing-only home services company (subcontracted)
one_liner: Generate and sell jobs such as roofing under your own brand and subcontract all of the work, so the business owns only the phone and the marketing.
customer: Homeowners who need roofing or similar trades
offer: A home service job delivered by vetted subcontractors
how_it_makes_money: Margin between the price charged to the customer and the subcontractor's cost
evidence: "My roofing company... we don't have a truck. We only have the phone because we're just marketing" (ZamYEo_mvxk)
A company did $9.8M in its first 90 days, 100% from organic Facebook Marketplace posts (ZamYEo_mvxk, a different business)
risks: Quality control and liability for subcontracted work
No margin figures given
The suggested tactic of fake Facebook accounts breaks platform rules and should be avoided

name: Form-factor product testing with AI ads
one_liner: Test demand for a proven product in a new form (gummies, powder, a better-looking rucking backpack) using AI-generated ad creative before buying any inventory.
offer: A redesigned consumer product, such as a non-tactical-looking rucking backpack
how_it_makes_money: DTC product sales, validated first with cheap AI ad creative
startup_cost: low to test, high to launch (inventory and ads)
evidence: Idea only: ads made for a rucking backpack with the line "start rucking without looking like a sniper". Weak evidence, no revenue (ZBVYDM8K8tA)
risks: No demand data
Inventory and ad costs once it scales
The transcript says ecom at $20K/month needs inventory and ads (XctiWvrRqkI)

name: Government surplus vehicle broker
one_liner: Find buyers for cheaply auctioned government surplus vehicles (ambulances, fire trucks, electric buses) and earn a finder's fee or resale margin.
customer: Businesses and individuals who need specialist vehicles
startup_cost: low if brokering, high if buying the vehicles
evidence: Full electric buses sold for between $2,500 and $25,000: "You could start a business just finding buyers for these." Weak evidence, no case shown (W5oUjuoHWhA)
risks: Mentioned only in passing
The UK and EU surplus market differs
Logistics and regulation for moving large vehicles
